# lazydap

> A scriptable, terminal-first debugger. Every debug operation is a shell subcommand that
> prints JSON, so anything that can run a command can inspect a running program. Wraps
> codelldb, so it debugs C, C++ and Rust. Pre-release: v0.1.0 is not tagged and there are no
> published binaries.

The one rule for driving it from code: put `--wait` on every command that moves the program
(`launch`, `continue`, `step`, `step-in`, `step-out`, `pause`). Without it the command returns
before the program has gone anywhere and you read a stale stack. With it you get one JSON
object describing the whole trip, including everything the program printed.

Read `state` to learn what happened to the program (`paused`, `exited`, `terminated`,
`timeout`, `adapter_died`). Read the process exit code to learn whether the command worked.
They answer different questions.

Any page on this site is available as Markdown by appending `.md` to its path. The whole
corpus is at /llms-full.txt.

## Known limitations

C, C++ and Rust via codelldb; Python via debugpy. No Go or Node yet. One session per
project at a time. macOS and Linux; Windows is not a target. Adapter discovery is config-pin
then PATH. No attach or restart. Breakpoint conditions, hit counts and log points are
CLI-only; the TUI's `b` sets a plain one. `variables_reference` values expire whenever the
program moves.
